## The Ground Is Part of the Conversation {#sec-lay-ch16}

## A Concrete Picture

Jump from a small boat and the boat slides backward. Push against a wall and the
wall returns a force through your body. Walking, throwing, and swinging all rely
on external contact with the environment. The ground is not merely a stage; it
is one boundary through which force and sometimes power enter the body.

Force plates make this interaction visible, but their curves are easy to
overinterpret. A vertical-force peak does not identify which muscle created it.
A center-of-pressure shift does not prove a unique segment sequence. The ground
reaction is a measured boundary load. A model must reproduce it consistently with
the measured motion, inertias, gravity, and other external loads; that consistency
does not identify the muscles that produced the motion.

![A Model Decomposes Net Reaction; a Summed Wrench Alone Leaves Foot Allocation Unresolved.](figures/proximal_distal_companion/fig_companion_ground_reaction_ledger.svg){#fig-lay-ground-ledger width=97% fig-alt="Four boxes for configuration, velocity-dependent drift, controls, and external loads feed a modeled net ground-reaction wrench, then branch to unresolved left and right foot allocations."}

## How the Mechanism Works

In an ideal constrained-contact model, ground reactions appear as multipliers
enforcing the selected contact constraints. Solving the equations can decompose reaction at a fixed state into
configuration/gravity, velocity-dependent, control, and external-load terms.
The technical study defines ground-reaction versions of zero-torque and
zero-velocity counterfactual forces.

### The Reaction Reflects the Whole System

Accelerating the club changes body reactions. Body motion changes required foot
forces. Gravity contributes. If the feet are constrained, the solver finds a
reaction satisfying both motion and contact. A large ground force is not a
separate motor delivering energy directly to the club; it is part of the
coupled external interaction.

Ground power depends on motion at the physical boundary. For a rigid contact
wrench referred to point $O$, in one observer frame,

$$
P_g=\mathbf F_g\cdot\mathbf v_O+
\mathbf M_{g,O}\cdot\boldsymbol\omega.
$$

The moment and velocity must refer to the same point on the same rigid body.
An ideal nonslipping rigid contact at rest in the chosen observer frame has zero boundary power despite
large reactions. For a deforming foot, use traction dotted with local
material-point velocity over the contact surface, including any applied contact
couples in the chosen continuum model. A center-of-pressure path is a changing
force-resultant location, not a material trajectory: its migration alone is not
ground work. Internal muscle, joint, and tissue work can occur while the external
ground port does zero work. A force plate measures wrench, not metabolic source.

### ZTCF Family and ZVCF Ask Narrow Questions

At one achieved state, the ground-reaction ZTCF sets declared controls to zero
and recomputes reaction. In the pinned technical study, ZVCF sets **both velocity
and declared control to zero**, retaining configuration and declared other loads.
Keeping control while zeroing velocity is the separate **zero-velocity
control-preserved reaction**. These pointwise calculations do not advance a
new trajectory or describe a person instantaneously stopping all motion.

In a fixed-support double-pendulum benchmark, pointwise ZTCF predicts the general
reaction waveform but retains substantial amplitude error. Opposing control can
make one ZTCF impulse exceed the total because contributions cancel. This is a
useful warning against treating a component as a measured fraction.

### Two Feet Add Allocation Ambiguity

A single net wrench under the body may be distributed across left and right feet
in many ways, especially if both contact regions can support moments. Separate
plates reduce ambiguity. Pressure insoles add spatial information. Yet foot
models, friction, and coordinate transforms remain.

The same common/differential logic used for hands applies to a summed wrench:
its net value does not specify its split. Separate six-axis plates directly
resolve each foot's aggregate wrench within measurement uncertainty, though
neither plate uniquely resolves within-foot pressure or muscle co-contraction.
Two feet do not automatically make every forward dynamics problem indeterminate;
constraint rank and the contact constitutive law determine that question.

### What Ground Data Can Test

Synchronized whole-body kinematics, separate force plates, club motion, and
bilateral grip wrenches can test the predicted **total** reaction in timing,
direction, and amplitude. Individual counterfactual components are not separately
measured by a plate. Their attribution requires additional model assumptions and
perturbation predictions. Residual forces and moments can expose inconsistencies in
segment parameters or filtering. Participant holdout tests whether a fitted
pattern generalizes.

**Model Result:** The fixed-support benchmark establishes a reproducible reaction
decomposition with partial waveform agreement and explicit amplitude limitations.

**Human Evidence:** Han and colleagues studied 63 skilled men, with handicap at
most 3, using optical motion capture and two force plates for driver, 5-iron,
and pitching-wedge shots. Their abstract reports associations between selected
force/moment peaks and maximum clubhead speed, not a muscle-level causal
decomposition [@han2019]. Ball and Best identified two major direction-of-hit
COP clusters in 62 golfers; this does not establish two exhaustive patterns of
two-dimensional foot pressure [@ballbest2007]. A 2026 systematic review retained
24 studies, mostly cross-sectional, and identified inconsistent methods and
remaining reliability and intervention questions [@watson2026grf]. These studies
measure different quantities and populations; none validates the present
counterfactual decomposition in humans.

**Hypothesis:** State-dependent reaction components may explain part of observed
ground-force timing without requiring each peak to be directly commanded, but
full-body human data must test the prediction.

**Practical Interpretation:** The ground tells us what net external conversation
occurred at the feet. It does not provide a transcript assigning every sentence
to a muscle.

### Force Plates Measure a Net External Wrench

A six-axis force plate reports three force components and three moments at its
declared origin. Transform these to the support surface before deriving COP.
For a planar surface $z=0$, reaction on the golfer, and $F_z\ne0$,
$x_{\rm COP}=-M_y/F_z$ and $y_{\rm COP}=M_x/F_z$; the remaining
$M_z-(x_{\rm COP}F_y-y_{\rm COP}F_x)$ is the surface-normal free moment.
Declare axes and signs, and mask low-load intervals where the ratios are unstable.
Separate plates preserve left--right aggregate allocation. Pressure insoles
usually measure normal pressure; shear and a full wrench require additional
sensing or a qualified model.

The plate does not report muscle force, joint torque, or energy “from the ground.”
It reports the reaction required at the contact boundary. To understand how that
reaction relates to the club, synchronize it with body and club motion and solve
the dynamics with uncertainty.

### Large Force Does Not Necessarily Mean Large Power

At an ideal stationary rigid support, both terms in the wrench-power expression
vanish. Body kinetic energy can still increase through active muscle work,
gravitational potential decrease, or release of elastic storage. Which changes
count as new mechanical input depends on the declared energy boundary. Force
magnitude is not an energy-flow rate, and a kinetic-energy increase alone does
not establish new active work.

This is similar to pushing a locked wall during a squat. The wall or ground
provides a reaction that permits body acceleration, while chemical energy in
muscle supplies work. Saying the golfer “gets energy from the ground” can be a
useful cue, but it is not a precise mechanical ledger unless contact work is
actually calculated.

### A Whole-Body Reaction Walkthrough

Early in the downswing, changes in pelvis and trunk motion require horizontal,
vertical, and rotational ground reactions. As arms and club accelerate, their
momentum changes alter the reaction needed by the rest of the system. Late club
acceleration can therefore appear in foot-force features even when no new foot
command specifically targets the club.

The influence is reciprocal. Ground reaction enables changes in whole-body
momentum that shape proximal motion, and distal acceleration changes the
reaction required for balance and constraint. Cross-correlation of peaks cannot
determine direction of causation. A forward model and perturbations are needed.

### Pointwise Ground-Reaction Decomposition

For an autonomous holonomic contact model, write

$$
\begin{aligned}
M\ddot q+h_0+h_v&=Bu+Q_e+J^\mathsf T\lambda,\\
J\ddot q+\gamma&=0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $h_0$ is the declared velocity-independent bias, $h_v$ the velocity bias,
$Bu$ the selected control, and $Q_e$ other loads. With positive-definite $M$
and $J$ of full row rank, let $A=JM^{-1}J^\mathsf T$. A well-conditioned linear
solve yields

$$
A\lambda=JM^{-1}(h_0+h_v-Bu-Q_e)-\gamma.
$$

Holding configuration, contact rows, and the declared load conventions fixed
gives an additive split $\lambda=\lambda_0+\lambda_v+\lambda_u+\lambda_e$.
ZTCF retains $\lambda_0+\lambda_v+\lambda_e$; ZVCF retains
$\lambda_0+\lambda_e$ when $h_v(q,0)=\gamma(q,0)=0$. Thus total minus ZTCF
isolates the declared control term, and ZTCF minus ZVCF isolates the velocity
term. **ZTCF and ZVCF overlap and are not additive parts of the total.**

Time-dependent constraints, velocity-dependent controllers or other loads,
slip, and contact opening require recomputation under the actual intervention.
They cannot inherit this fixed-operator shortcut without qualification.
Compute COP from each reconstructed wrench; dividing each component separately
does not produce an additive COP decomposition.

Components can cancel, so a counterfactual reaction may exceed total in one
direction. That does not mean it contributed more than one hundred percent of a
measured force. It means another component opposed it. Report signed waveforms,
impulses, cancellation, and residual rather than forcing an additive percentage
story.

### Two Feet Create an Allocation Problem

The same net body wrench may be supported by different left and right contact
wrenches within friction and balance constraints. Separate plates observe much
of this allocation. If both feet occupy one plate, a model or pressure data must
supply the split, and nonuniqueness should be shown.

Foot models also need contact assumptions. A fixed point, rolling contact,
distributed pressure, and compliant shoe produce different reaction paths. The
choice should match the measurement question. A mechanism that depends on an
unrealistic fixed foot may not survive a richer contact rung.

### Connecting Ground and Hand Ledgers

For the **body-plus-club** system before ball impact, ground, gravity, and any
other external contacts or aerodynamic loads determine total momentum change.
Hand--club interface loads are internal: include both sides with consistent
points and signs, so their complete wrench cancels. For the body alone, the
club-on-hand wrench is external; for the club alone, the opposite wrench is
external. Do not add hand loads again to the combined-system external ledger.

About a fixed inertial origin $O$, $\dot{\mathbf H}_O$ equals the total external
moment about $O$. If the reporting origin moves, include the transport term
appropriate to the chosen angular-momentum definition. Segment powers and
internal elastic/dissipative storage then connect the system ledger to the
hand interface; action--reaction alone does not make internal work vanish.

This creates powerful error checks. If measured hand and ground loads combined
with motion leave large residuals, segment inertias, filtering, synchronization,
or unmeasured contacts may be wrong. A polished transfer story should wait until
those residuals are bounded.

### What Ground Manipulations Could Test

Researchers can compare stance width, lead/trail pressure constraints, surface
friction within safe limits, or externally paced tempo while measuring the
predicted hand and club mediators. The mechanism should specify whether changing
a ground variable shifts proximal state, hand wrench, negative-couple interval,
or only balance strategy.

A finding that ground-force peaks change without the predicted hand or club
change would weaken a simple ground-to-club transfer narrative. A finding that
hand-wrench timing mediates the relation would strengthen the chain. Participant
holdout is essential because people may adopt different compensations.

### Practical Boundary

Force-plate patterns can characterize an individual and expose constraints, but
they should not become universal target traces. Similar club outcomes can arise
from different foot allocations, and larger peaks can reflect braking or balance
as readily as useful propulsion. The valuable question is how the measured
external wrench fits the complete system ledger and whether a proposed change
improves robust outcomes without unacceptable load.

### Reader Lab: Close the External Wrench

Take synchronized body and club kinematics, segment parameters, separate foot
wrenches, gravity, and any other external loads. Compute body-plus-club linear
and angular momentum change and compare with integrated external wrench about
a fixed inertial origin. Use hand measurements to close the body and club
subsystems separately, without double-counting them in the combined system. Plot residual by
direction and phase. A large residual near peak club acceleration may reflect
synchronization, filtering, inertia, or omitted contact—not a new force.

Next sum the two foot plates and verify the result against a single combined
wrench calculation. Shift reference point consistently. Compute center of
pressure only when vertical force and moment assumptions make it well defined.
Flag low-force intervals rather than allowing unstable ratios.

Finally, validate the total modeled reaction against the plates and run the
declared pointwise counterfactuals. Show component timing as model attribution.
A component-to-total difference is not itself a validation error: the other
components are expected to contribute. Test counterfactual predictions through
separately specified perturbations and held-out trials.

### Competing Explanations for a Force Peak

A vertical peak can reflect accelerating the body center of mass, resisting
downward motion, club reaction, balance, or a combination. A horizontal peak can
turn or translate the system. A free moment can relate to rotational balance but
does not map uniquely to pelvis or club torque.

Test proposed pathways with mediation and intervention. If a stance manipulation
changes ground force but neither proximal state nor hand wrench as predicted,
the simple transfer chain is unsupported. If all links change in order and a
forward model predicts them on held-out trials, the explanation strengthens.

### From an Observation to a Causal Claim

Suppose higher club speed is associated with a larger lead-side vertical impulse.
That is an observation. A causal hypothesis might say the impulse changes pelvis
and trunk state, which changes hand wrench and later club acceleration. The
hypothesis requires each mediator and its timing. A model can predict the chain;
a manipulation and synchronized data can test it.

Alternative explanations include stronger golfers producing both variables,
different stance or club, balance response to the faster club, or processing
choices. Randomized safe manipulations, within-person contrasts, and held-out
prediction reduce these alternatives. The ground trace alone cannot.

### What the Product Should Display

Show separate and summed foot wrenches, center of pressure only in valid
intervals, whole-system momentum residual, predicted reaction components, and
uncertainty. Link peaks to concurrent body, hand, and club state. Let readers
toggle pointwise ZTCF and ZVCF components while explaining that they are model
counterfactuals.

Do not rank a golfer from force magnitude alone. Normalize only when the
scientific comparison justifies it and retain dimensional values. A transparent
display should make cancellation, allocation ambiguity, and residuals as visible
as the headline pattern.

### A Final Ground Check

For a closed accounting of kinetic, gravitational, and elastic mechanical energy,
any increase must be supplied by declared active work or external ports, with
dissipation also recorded. Release of already-counted elastic storage redistributes
that energy; it does not create it. If the support is compliant, specify whether
its stored energy belongs inside the system or enters through an external port.
This keeps everyday “use the ground” language tied to an explicit ledger.

### What Happened When the Ground Was Actually Added

The archived finite-base experiment adds horizontal/vertical translation, pitch
about world $y$, or both to an articulated model. Each pathway is paired with
the fixed-base version at the same registered initial state. Its intrinsic
**pitch moment** differs from a force plate's usual surface-normal free moment.
The support law is linear spring--damper mechanics, without two feet,
unilateral ground contact, Coulomb friction, or measured plantar pressure.

The design comprises 12 states, four primary pathways, two signed initial
velocity perturbations, two timesteps, and two native dynamics backends:
$12\times4\times2\times2\times2=384$ primary trajectories. Two control families
add 192 trajectories. Each is summarized at 4, 10, 25, and 50 ms, giving 1536
primary pathway summaries. The coupled-versus-fixed subset contains 96 trajectory
pairs, each compared at four horizons. Consequently, it has **384 summary comparisons**,
$12\times2\times2\times2\times4$, rather than 384 independent human trials or
384 distinct trajectory pairs. Engine and timestep variants are numerical
replications of the modeled conditions.

MuJoCo and Pinocchio supply independent native dynamics operators but use a
**shared contact law** and semi-implicit integration in this experiment. The
maximum archived trajectory relative discrepancy is about $1.77\times10^{-10}$.
The worst primary normalized energy residual decreases from about 0.01986 to
0.00995 when the timestep halves. These results support implementation agreement
and refinement over the sampled domain; they are not independent validation of
all contact physics. All primary and control numerical gates pass, while the
separate load/work matching criterion fails.

### What the Matching Criterion Actually Measures

The archive's **declared primary criterion** requires both peak grip load and
total dissipated work to match within 5%. Here load is the maximum single-station
force norm over the interval, not the summed hand force. A separate timestamped prospective
registration was not verified here. The work comparison is

$$
\delta_W=\frac{|W_c-W_f|}
{\max(10^{-6}\,\mathrm J,(|W_c|+|W_f|)/2)},
$$

where $c$ and $f$ denote coupled and fixed support and $W$ is nonnegative
dissipated work. Peak load uses the same symmetric normalization with a 1 N
floor. **Zero of 384** comparisons meet both criteria; 202 meet the load
criterion alone. The work discrepancy ranges from 1.723 to 1.999. This does
**not** mean twice as much energy. With positive work and no active floor,
the symmetric discrepancy approaches 2 as the ratio diverges. The actual
coupled/fixed work ratios range from **13.44 to 3519.40**. Small fixed-base
dissipation makes a large ratio possible; the archived fixed and coupled ranges
are approximately $4.46\times10^{-7}$--0.00290 J and 0.00157--1.872 J.

The sampled tolerance sweep finds no matches through 100% and all 384 at 200%.
For nonnegative quantities this symmetric discrepancy cannot exceed 200%, so
that last threshold imposes no meaningful matching requirement. It is not an
estimated minimum tolerance, nor proof that unequal work is unavoidable in every
possible ground model. Adding support damping changes dissipation directly and
also changes motion, hence grip and shaft dissipation.

The supported conclusion is narrow: **no eligible comparison exists to estimate
a speed benefit under the joint load-and-total-work matching criterion**. An
empty matched cohort does not estimate a zero effect. That criterion must
not be replaced silently after seeing the result.

### A Total Simulated Contrast Is a Different Question

At the finer timestep and 50 ms, the coupled pathway has higher terminal club
translation speed in all 48 summaries, by approximately 0.028--0.177 m/s. These
are 12 states, two velocity signs, and two backends. The atlas has no active
driver or joint torque; motion begins from the assigned state and perturbation,
with initial mechanical energy matched across pathways.

Changing support alters the equations, energy redistribution, and losses. The
resulting paired trajectory difference is a **total effect of that declared
model intervention**. Dissipation is partly downstream of the support change,
so equalizing it would ask a different question. Failing the matching screen
does not erase the total simulated contrast; conversely, the contrast does not
establish an equal-load/equal-work advantage, optimal coordination, energy
supplied by stationary ground, or a causal benefit in golfers. The modeled
endpoint is 50 ms translation speed, not impact speed or whole-swing performance.

A post-hoc sensitivity excludes ground damping from the matched-work quantity
while retaining grip and shaft dissipation. It finds 60 matches: **48, 8, 4, and 0**
at 4, 10, 25, and 50 ms respectively, across both steps and backends. Their speed
differences range from approximately −0.00075 to +0.01394 m/s, with 20 positive
and 40 negative. These are not 60 successful 50 ms comparisons. This alternative
estimand remains exploratory and does not replace the primary result.

### Initialization Is Part of the Experiment

A separate 4 ms diagnostic uses seven branches, three steps, and two backends:
42 trajectories. At the 0.125 ms step, three coupled-support initializations give
the following peak ground forces and terminal club translation speeds:

| Initialization | Force (N) | Speed (m/s) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Natural-Zero | 32.8 | 0.264 |
| Gravity-Only | 565.5 | 1.908 |
| Conditional Base | 510.3 | 0.946 |

Natural-zero matches the registered initial coordinates and energy but is not
static equilibrium. Gravity-only balance omits the grip preload contribution.
Conditional equilibrium balances the three base coordinates while holding the
remaining posture and club fixed; it is not equilibrium of every coordinate.
The resulting initial storage and transients differ, so these numbers demonstrate
initialization sensitivity, not three human standing strategies.

This archive also uses distributed central tension-only grip fibers. Their
equal-and-opposite endpoint forces have zero combined pair moment. The
noncentral vector-dashpot limitation discussed in @sec-lay-ch20 belongs to a
different archived pathway and must not be attributed to these fibers.

### Chapter Checkpoint

Ground reaction is external force evidence, not a muscle transcript or automatic
energy source. Use it to close momentum, test contact models, and constrain the
causal chain through body and hands. Report left/right allocation and model
components without converting them into additive percentages.

And when someone shows you a speed difference between a moving base and a fixed
one, ask what was held equal before the comparison was made.

A practical pattern becomes mechanistically meaningful only when its predicted
mediators and outcome survive within-person manipulation and participant holdout.

## Where the Picture Breaks

The wall and boat pictures use simple rigid contacts. Feet roll, deform, slip
microscopically, and distribute pressure. Fixed-support pendulums omit balance,
pelvis translation, and bilateral contact.

Correlation between force peaks and segment motion cannot establish causation.
Timing can reflect shared state, feedback, or filtering. Reaction decomposition
must be validated against synchronized data before becoming a human claim.
